blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.22
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.22

blocks.text: प्राणसमाचारे समदर्शनम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] प्राणसमाचारे समदर्शनम्

blocks.text: Prāṇasamācāre samadarśanam.
blocks.directed: Prāṇasamācāre samadarśanam.

blocks.text: When the vital power flows outward in an integrated way, there is equal vision of the one conscious reality.
blocks.directed: When the vital power flows outward in an integrated way, there is equal vision of the one conscious reality.

blocks.text: You Come Out of Samādhi, and the Entire World Is Still Śiva. Excellent.
blocks.directed: You Come Out of Samādhi, and the Entire World Is Still Śiva. Excellent.

blocks.text: Now this is magnificent.
blocks.directed: Now this is magnificent.

blocks.text: Because we’ve just entered the supreme condition through inward immersion.
blocks.directed: Because we’ve just entered the supreme condition through inward immersion.

blocks.text: And a very obvious question arises.
blocks.directed: And a very obvious question arises.

blocks.text: What happens when we come out?
blocks.directed: What happens when we come out?

blocks.text: Do we lose it?
blocks.directed: Do we lose it?

blocks.text: Does the world become alien again?
blocks.directed: Does the world become alien again?

blocks.text: Do we immediately return to the ordinary sense of separation?
blocks.directed: Do we immediately return to the ordinary sense of separation?

blocks.text: Do we have to spend the rest of our lives sitting perfectly still, hoping nobody disturbs us?
blocks.directed: Do we have to spend the rest of our lives sitting perfectly still, hoping nobody disturbs us?

blocks.text: Well, Vasugupta has a much more interesting answer.
blocks.directed: Well, Vasugupta has a much more interesting answer.

blocks.text: Samadarśanam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Samadarśanam.

blocks.text: Equal vision.
blocks.directed: Equal vision.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Prāṇa — vital breath or vital energy.
blocks.directed: Prāṇa — vital breath or vital energy.

blocks.text: Samācāra — proper, balanced or integrated movement; here, the gradual outward extension of vital activity.
blocks.directed: Samācāra — proper, balanced or integrated movement; here, the gradual outward extension of vital activity.

blocks.text: Sama — equal, uniform, undivided in this context.
blocks.directed: Sama — equal, uniform, undivided in this context.

blocks.text: Darśana — seeing, vision, apprehension.
blocks.directed: Darśana — seeing, vision, apprehension.

blocks.text: Now, this is not simply a sūtra about breathing slowly.
blocks.directed: Now, this is not simply a sūtra about breathing slowly.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja’s commentary is much more specific.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja’s commentary is much more specific.

blocks.text: He explains that after the yogi enters the supreme state, vital activity naturally begins to extend outward again.
blocks.directed: He explains that after the yogi enters the supreme state, vital activity naturally begins to extend outward again.

blocks.text: The practitioner doesn’t remain permanently absorbed in a condition without ordinary engagement.
blocks.directed: The practitioner doesn’t remain permanently absorbed in a condition without ordinary engagement.

blocks.text: The senses operate.
blocks.directed: The senses operate.

blocks.text: The breath moves.
blocks.directed: The breath moves.

blocks.text: The mind functions.
blocks.directed: The mind functions.

blocks.text: The world appears.
blocks.directed: The world appears.

blocks.text: But now the outgoing activity is pervaded by the recognition of supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: But now the outgoing activity is pervaded by the recognition of supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: And therefore samadarśana arises.
blocks.directed: And therefore samadarśana arises.

blocks.text: The yogi perceives the same fundamental reality throughout experience.
blocks.directed: The yogi perceives the same fundamental reality throughout experience.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja describes this as the uniformity of cidānanda.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja describes this as the uniformity of cidānanda.

blocks.text: Consciousness and bliss.
blocks.directed: Consciousness and bliss.

blocks.text: And this is important.
blocks.directed: And this is important.

blocks.text: The yogi doesn’t merely have an extraordinary experience and then return to a fundamentally separate ordinary life.
blocks.directed: The yogi doesn’t merely have an extraordinary experience and then return to a fundamentally separate ordinary life.

blocks.text: The recognition becomes operative as experience unfolds again.
blocks.directed: The recognition becomes operative as experience unfolds again.

blocks.text: Now imagine someone meditating.
blocks.directed: Now imagine someone meditating.

blocks.text: The mind becomes quiet.
blocks.directed: The mind becomes quiet.

blocks.text: The sense of limitation temporarily subsides.
blocks.directed: The sense of limitation temporarily subsides.

blocks.text: There’s an extraordinary experience of spaciousness.
blocks.directed: There’s an extraordinary experience of spaciousness.

blocks.text: And then they open their eyes.
blocks.directed: And then they open their eyes.

blocks.text: There’s a table.
blocks.directed: There’s a table.

blocks.text: A chair.
blocks.directed: A chair.

blocks.text: Some dust floating in a beam of sunlight.
blocks.directed: Some dust floating in a beam of sunlight.

blocks.text: An irritating noise outside.
blocks.directed: An irritating noise outside.

blocks.text: And the question is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the question is:

blocks.text: Has the divine disappeared because objects have returned?
blocks.directed: Has the divine disappeared because objects have returned?

blocks.text: From the Trika standpoint, no.
blocks.directed: From the Trika standpoint, no.

blocks.text: Because the objects themselves are manifestations of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Because the objects themselves are manifestations of consciousness.

blocks.text: The apparent distinction between meditation and ordinary experience doesn’t establish two fundamentally different ultimate realities.
blocks.directed: The apparent distinction between meditation and ordinary experience doesn’t establish two fundamentally different ultimate realities.

blocks.text: The supreme conscious nature is not restricted to the absence of objects.
blocks.directed: The supreme conscious nature is not restricted to the absence of objects.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja makes precisely this point.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja makes precisely this point.

blocks.text: He explains that even as the intellect and prāṇa extend towards external objects, the realised yogi remains established in universal consciousness without the contracted standpoint returning.
blocks.directed: He explains that even as the intellect and prāṇa extend towards external objects, the realised yogi remains established in universal consciousness without the contracted standpoint returning.

blocks.text: He cites the Pratyabhijñā tradition and a passage associated with Ānandabhairava concerning equal vision across divine beings, social distinctions and things. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He cites the Pratyabhijñā tradition and a passage associated with Ānandabhairava concerning equal vision across divine beings, social distinctions and things. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now let’s be careful.
blocks.directed: Now let’s be careful.

blocks.text: Equal vision doesn’t mean empirical differences cease to matter.
blocks.directed: Equal vision doesn’t mean empirical differences cease to matter.

blocks.text: A tiger and a cup of tea remain very different things.
blocks.directed: A tiger and a cup of tea remain very different things.

blocks.text: And treating them identically could lead to a rather unpleasant afternoon.
blocks.directed: And treating them identically could lead to a rather unpleasant afternoon.

blocks.text: It doesn’t mean morality disappears.
blocks.directed: It doesn’t mean morality disappears.

blocks.text: Nor that harmful actions become acceptable merely because everything is Śiva.
blocks.directed: Nor that harmful actions become acceptable merely because everything is Śiva.

blocks.text: The philosophical point is that the underlying conscious reality is not ultimately divided by the differentiated forms through which it manifests.
blocks.directed: The philosophical point is that the underlying conscious reality is not ultimately divided by the differentiated forms through which it manifests.

blocks.text: And here’s the extraordinary result.
blocks.directed: And here’s the extraordinary result.

blocks.text: The yogi can participate in the world without losing recognition of its source.
blocks.directed: The yogi can participate in the world without losing recognition of its source.

blocks.text: The senses function.
blocks.directed: The senses function.

blocks.text: The body functions.
blocks.directed: The body functions.

blocks.text: Speech occurs.
blocks.directed: Speech occurs.

blocks.text: Action occurs.
blocks.directed: Action occurs.

blocks.text: But their apparent differentiation no longer conceals the universal conscious reality.
blocks.directed: But their apparent differentiation no longer conceals the universal conscious reality.

blocks.text: This is integration.
blocks.directed: This is integration.

blocks.text: And it’s a profound contrast with the idea that liberation consists solely in withdrawing from the world.
blocks.directed: And it’s a profound contrast with the idea that liberation consists solely in withdrawing from the world.

blocks.text: The inward movement is important.
blocks.directed: The inward movement is important.

blocks.text: But so is the outward return.
blocks.directed: But so is the outward return.

blocks.text: The contemplative state and ordinary activity are not ultimately alien realities.
blocks.directed: The contemplative state and ordinary activity are not ultimately alien realities.

blocks.text: Now, this is where things become particularly relevant to the problem of stabilising recognition.
blocks.directed: Now, this is where things become particularly relevant to the problem of stabilising recognition.

blocks.text: Because Vasugupta is not claiming that everyone who has experienced turya will automatically remain established in it.
blocks.directed: Because Vasugupta is not claiming that everyone who has experienced turya will automatically remain established in it.

blocks.text: Quite the opposite.
blocks.directed: Quite the opposite.

blocks.text: The next two sūtras address what happens when the recognition becomes interrupted.
blocks.directed: The next two sūtras address what happens when the recognition becomes interrupted.

blocks.text: And they are absolutely brilliant.
blocks.directed: And they are absolutely brilliant.

blocks.text: Because we’re about to encounter something deeply familiar.
blocks.directed: Because we’re about to encounter something deeply familiar.

blocks.text: You recognise the truth.
blocks.directed: You recognise the truth.

blocks.text: You forget.
blocks.directed: You forget.

blocks.text: You remember again.
blocks.directed: You remember again.

blocks.text: You become distracted.
blocks.directed: You become distracted.

blocks.text: You recognise again.
blocks.directed: You recognise again.

blocks.text: And Vasugupta is going to explain the entire cycle through the relationship between the middle of experience and its conscious source.
blocks.directed: And Vasugupta is going to explain the entire cycle through the relationship between the middle of experience and its conscious source.

blocks.text: Which is exactly the sort of thing you’d expect from a man who has already informed us that the universe is an elaborate one-man theatrical production.
blocks.directed: Which is exactly the sort of thing you’d expect from a man who has already informed us that the universe is an elaborate one-man theatrical production.
